title: Ash-Shams: the soul
hook: by the soul and its shaping, successful is the one who purifies it (91:7–10)
carry: the one who purifies it succeeds

segments.voice: Yesterday: Ash-Shams, and a run of oaths from the sun down through the sky and the earth. Your line was by the sun. Did you stop and look at the light? Day one hundred ninety-two.

Sun. Moon. Day. Night. Sky. Earth. And then the last thing Ash-Shams swears by, something small enough to fit inside a person. Not a star, not a mountain. A soul. Yours, and everyone's. The whole sky was the windup. After all that buildup, the surah says one thing about the soul, one sentence about what success actually is. It isn't the kind of success that goes on a resume or into a headline. Today: the soul.
screen: `SUN, MOON, SKY, EARTH.` → `NOT A STAR. A SOUL.` → `WHAT SUCCESS ACTUALLY IS.`

segments.voice: Verse seven: by the soul, nafs, and the One who shaped it and made it well-proportioned. Verse eight: and inspired it with its wickedness and its mindfulness. Both, in the same soul, from the start. The surah doesn't pretend people are pure by default, or rotten by default. It says the soul knows both roads. Then the sentence the oaths were building to. In Pickthall's words: He is indeed successful who causeth it to grow. And the next verse, the mirror: the one who buries it, who stunts it, has failed. The Arabic verb for the first is zakkaha. You've heard the root: zakat, the giving that is one of the five pillars. Z-k-y carries two ideas at once, to purify and to grow, the way pruning a plant cleans it and makes it grow stronger. So zakat purifies wealth, and this verse says a person can do the same to a soul. The opposite verb, dassaha, means to bury something, to hide it in the dirt. Later scholars gave the work of the first verb a name, tazkiyah, purification of the soul. But the verse itself is plain. Success isn't money or followers here. It's what you did with the soul you were given: did you tend it, or bury it? The surah then ends with a short, sharp story, the people of Thamud who hamstrung the she-camel they'd been warned to leave alone. An example of a soul buried, a whole people at a time.
screen: `THE SOUL KNOWS BOTH ROADS.` · `ZAKKAHA — TO PURIFY AND TO GROW.` · `DASSAHA — TO BURY IT IN THE DIRT.` · `SUCCESS: WHAT YOU DID WITH IT.` · then, large: `THE ONE WHO PURIFIES IT SUCCEEDS.`

segments.voice: Sit, and for two minutes think of one small habit that clouds your day a little. The scroll before sleep. The sharp reply. The thing you say about a coworker. Just one, and small. Picture pruning it: one cut, not a whole new life. Decide what the cut looks like today. If you pray, you can ask for help with it in your own words. The bell holds the time.
Ash-Shams. The sun, Surah ninety-one, whose oaths end on the soul: successful is the one who purifies it. Today's word.
Your line: the one who purifies it succeeds. Make the one small cut you chose, once, today. Tending is done in small cuts. Day one hundred ninety-two.

howItsDone: Muslims speak of tazkiyah, the lifelong work of purifying the soul, through prayer, remembrance, charity and watching one's habits; the verse on success in Ash-Shams is often quoted about it.

match.prompt: what's inside the verses — tap the pairs.

myth: Ash-Shams says the soul starts out purely good
it says the soul was inspired with both its wickedness and its mindfulness.
the verb for purifying the soul shares a root with zakat
z-k-y: to purify and to grow, like pruning a plant.
the surah defines success as wealth and standing
success is the one who purifies the soul; failure is the one who buries it.

fork.setup: after its run of oaths, Ash-Shams names who is successful. who is it?
options: the one who is never tempted
the one who purifies the soul
the one who knows the most
fork.reveal: the one who makes it grow and purifies it (91:9). the soul knows both roads; success is what you tend.

original.note: Arabic: "purified it," from z-k-y, to purify and to grow, the root of zakat (Qur'an 91:9).

trapdoor: what you thought: be a good person.
what it means: the soul was given both roads; success is purifying it, failure is burying it.
what a scholar hears: zakkaha against dassaha, grow against bury; from this verse comes the vocabulary of tazkiyat al-nafs, the purification of the soul.

sources.quoted: He is indeed successful who causeth it to grow

sources.ref: Qur'an 91:7–8, 91:10 (the soul shaped and inspired; the one who stunts it)
